newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine minister sees labor accord in June.
newsitem.headline: Argentine minister sees labor accord in June.

text.p: Argentine unions, business and the government should reach a deal over a long- awaited package of labor law reforms by the end of the month, Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said Wednesday.
"A good date would be the end of this month," said Caro Figueroa, quoted by the state-controlled Telam news agency.
After months of disagreement, the government and the CGT labor federation reached a preliminary agreement on draft laws to reform the labor market in May.
But the deal was opposed by the Group of Eight business lobby, which argued that the reforms had been watered down.
Caro Figueroa said the Group of Eight was "showing a great will to negotiate."
The pact would replace severance payments with an unemployment insurance system and alter centralized wage bargaining to allow for some contracts to be directly negotiated between workers and firms.
But it would scale back earlier government plans to allow private health firms to compete with union health plans.
The government hopes that making Argentina's labor market more flexible will help reduce the country's 17.3 percent unemployment rate.
"This agreement would resolve problems which Argentina has been putting off for the last 50 years," Caro Figueroa said.
